children: Nifty IT index fell 0.6% on September 25 as crude prices above $100 a barrel intensified inflationary worries and bolstered bets on multiple Federal Reserve rate hikes in the near term.
Higher US rates could dent demand and economic growth in sectors exposed to the geography, such as Indian IT.

The Nifty IT was also the top laggard on the sectoral front. Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services were down 2% and 0.5%, respectively. These two were the key drags on the Nifty 50. In the mid-cap space, Oracle Financial Services Software shed 5% and was the top laggard in the Nifty 200 index. Oracle Financial's parent company had also closed over 3% lower in the US Thursday on reports that it has sent a force majeure notice to a developer of its data centre in New Mexico due to power-linked delays. Only HCL Technologies, LTM and Persistent Systems were trading in the green.
At 10:30 am on September 25, Nifty IT was trading 0.6% lower at 28,055.55, extending its decline for the sixth straight session. The index fell 4% during the period.

Expectations of higher-for-longer US interest rates firmed after two Fed policymakers said additional hikes may be needed to curb unacceptably high inflation, following last week's quarter-point increase in the benchmark rate.

"Returning inflation to 2% is a top priority, and I will support the policy path that gets us there while carefully weighing risks to the labour market along the way," Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson said. New York Fed President John Williams also suggested tighter monetary policy is coming.
Markets are currently pricing in a nearly 69% probability of a US rate hike in October, according to CME's FedWatch Tool.

Markets have aggressively repriced the interest rate trajectory after the Fed tightened policy last week, while robust economic data and fresh energy supply concerns have further strengthened that conviction. A bond selloff, which sent long-dated US Treasury yields to their highest in more than 20 years, also gave the greenback a leg up.

The dollar index, which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, has climbed more than 1% this week to a two-month high, marking its first back-to-back weekly gains since June. However, the rally was losing some momentum, last edging a touch lower at 101.2.

title: IT shares fall for sixth straight session; OFSS, Infosys top losers: Here's why
